column4: The source's root خ ش ع describes lowered faces; 41:39 calls the earth خَاشِعَةً before rain stirs it and revives it, joining the same root to an earth-to-life reversal.
The source's dictionary note for root ض ر ع links it to abasement; 6:63 says people call on God تَضَرُّعًا when endangered at sea, a concrete humility under distress.
The same root ض ر ع appears in the command to call God تَضَرُّعًا and privately; this is chosen humility, set beside the source's imposed abasement.
Zechariah's family hasten to good works, call on God in hope and fear, and are خَاشِعِينَ to Him; this gives the source's lowered-face root a voluntary devotional form.
When revelation is recited, people fall on their chins weeping and their humility increases; this gives the source's root خ ش ع a chosen bodily lowering.
The faithful women and men are among the خَاشِعِينَ; the same root that describes the source's lowered faces can name a chosen quality of worship.
Those who believe in God's signs fall prostrate and are not arrogant; this links voluntary lowering to the refusal of self-elevation that the source contrasts with the humiliated end.
When God's signs are recited, the prophets fall prostrate and weep; this is a chosen low posture, unlike the source's faces lowered by judgment.
70:43 shows people emerging rapidly from graves toward the caller; 70:44 supplies the humbled eyes, so this verse adds the movement into the source's judgment scene.
People are called to prostrate but cannot in 68:42; 68:43 names their humbled eyes and disgrace, making refusal the immediate cause of the source-like abasement.
Hearts tremble in 79:8, and 79:9 supplies the humbled eyes; this verse identifies the inner fear behind the source's lowered face.
After humbled eyes and emergence from graves in 54:7, 54:8 has people hasten toward the caller and call it a difficult day; it completes the source's resurrection posture.
The source says the person is seated high while only the cups are placed low; 16:58 shows a daughter's birth treated as disgrace, a human being wrongly pushed into low social standing.

16:59 makes the social abasement explicit by weighing whether to keep the daughter in humiliation or bury her in dust; it supplies the human-side reversal to the source's placement of objects below honored people.
The arrogant are barred from the Garden until a camel passes through a needle's eye; the source's pride branch for root ك ب ر thus meets an explicit boundary to its high Garden.
When told to fear God, the arrogant person is carried by pride into sin and Hell; this ties the source's self-greatening sense of ك ب ر to its great punishment.
God says not to grieve over what is missed or exult over what He gives, since He dislikes the boastful; this directly limits the self-awarded elevation warned of in the source.
The root ك ب ر appears in God's name الْمُتَكَبِّرُ; this locates true greatness with God and bounds the source's warning about people claiming height for themselves.
The verse calls God الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ, joining the source's named roots ع ل و and ك ب ر as divine attributes rather than human self-elevation.
The command to magnify God uses the root ك ب ر in reverent glorification; it gives the source's pride branch a clear counterpart in greatness rightly directed to God.
The sky is a protected ceiling in 21:32; this gives the source's raised-heaven image a boundary and sheltering function above the earth.
15:19 says the earth is spread and plants grow from it; it repeats the source's ground image while connecting the surface to provision.
The oath names the sky and its builder; 91:6 completes it with the spread earth, closely pairing the two elements that the source sets high and low.
The earth is spread in 91:6; 91:5 supplies the sky and its builder, completing the source's sky-earth pairing.
At the end, the earth is extended in 84:3; this reverses the source's stable spread-earth scene into the day of judgment.
84:4 says the earth casts out what is within and becomes empty; it explains the judgment-time extension in 84:3 and turns the source's ground into a scene of disclosure.
The earth listens to and obeys its Lord in 84:5; this completes the extended-earth sequence with submission to the Lord who orders the source's high and low.
The earth is shaken violently when the Hour arrives; this makes the source's spread ground undergo an explicit eschatological reversal.
The earth casts out its burdens in 99:2; the next verse has humanity ask what is happening, so this adds the ground's testimony to the source's judgment scene.
Earth and mountains are lifted and crushed in one blow; this turns the source's ordered high sky and spread earth into a judgment-time upheaval.
The sky splits on that day in 69:16; this reverses the source's raised, stable heaven at the end.
God holds the sky from falling on earth except by His permission; this specifies the boundary between the source's upper sky and lower ground.
The Garden's people recline on couches, protected from sun and cold; this expands the source's raised resting place into an environment of ease.
The Garden's people have abundant fruit to eat in 43:73; this adds a specific food-side counterpart to the source's punitive food.
The Garden's drink is mixed with ginger in 76:17; this develops the cup service parallel to the source's placed vessels.
The drink comes from a spring called Salsabil in 76:18; this adds a Garden spring to the source's cups and high seating.
Young attendants circulate among the Garden's people in 76:19; this makes explicit the service relation implicit in the source's low-placed cups and honored occupants.
The Garden's group sits facing one another on couches in 56:16; this continues the source's raised-seat scene with its social arrangement.
The Garden's people sit facing one another on couches in 37:44; this repeats the source's elevated seat as a setting for companionship.
